entry.summary: Presents the first systematic study of 4-bit quantization-aware training for attention mechanisms, identifying key principles for stable FP4 attention and proposing Attn-QAT to enable end-to-end FP4 computation on emerging hardware.

entry.title: Reverse CAPTCHA: Evaluating LLM Susceptibility to Invisible Unicode Instruction Injection

author.name: Marcus Graves

entry.summary: Reverse CAPTCHA evaluates LLM susceptibility to invisible Unicode-encoded instructions, finding that tool use dramatically amplifies compliance with hidden instructions (Cohen's h up to 1.37) and models show provider-specific encoding preferences.

entry.title: LangGap: Diagnosing and Closing the Language Gap in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yuchen Hou, Lin Zhao

entry.summary: LangGap reveals that state-of-the-art Vision-Language-Action models largely ignore language instructions, achieving >95% on standard benchmarks but failing when tasks require actual language understanding. Proposes the LangGap benchmark.

entry.title: The Expressive Limits of Diagonal SSMs for State-Tracking

author.name: Mehran Shakerinava, Behnoush Khavari, Siamak Ravanbakhsh, Sarath Chandar

entry.summary: Precisely characterizes the expressivity of diagonal state-space models for state-tracking tasks: k-layer DCD SSMs can express state-tracking of a group iff it has a subnormal series of length k with Abelian factors.

entry.title: Multi-Head Low-Rank Attention

author.name: Songtao Liu, Hongwu Peng, Zhiwei Zhang, Zhengyu Chen, Yue Guo

entry.summary: Proposes Multi-Head Low-Rank Attention (MHLRA) to address the sharding bottleneck of Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) in distributed decoding, enabling better tensor parallelism for KV cache management.

entry.title: Context Awareness: Constitutional AI can mitigate Emergent Misalignement

author.name: Giuseppe Birardi

entry.summary: Empirical study showing that Constitutional AI-style character training reduces emergent misalignment (EM) across multiple persona types on Qwen 2.5 7B and Llama 3.1 8B. Finds that even safety-irrelevant personas (humor, poetry) confer protection, and custom metacommunicative constitutions achieve the lowest misalignment rates. Notes model-dependent effects where sarcasm training amplifies misalignment on Llama but not Qwen.

entry.title: How Well Does Agent Development Reflect Real-World Work?

author.name: Zora Zhiruo Wang, Sanidhya Vijayvargiya, Aspen Chen, Hanmo Zhang, Venu Arvind Arangarajan, Jett Chen, Valerie Chen, Diyi Yang, Daniel Fried, Graham Neubig

entry.summary: Systematically maps 43 agent benchmarks (72,342 tasks) to real-world occupations in the U.S. labor market, revealing substantial mismatches between programming-centric agent development and where human labor/economic value concentrate.

entry.title: What Is the Geometry of the Alignment Tax?

author.name: Robin Young

entry.summary: Provides a geometric theory of the alignment tax, defining it as the squared projection of the safety direction onto the capability subspace and deriving the Pareto frontier for safety-capability tradeoffs parameterized by principal angles.

entry.title: Formal Analysis and Supply Chain Security for Agentic AI Skills

author.name: Varun Pratap Bhardwaj

entry.summary: SkillFortify provides formal analysis for agent skill supply chains, responding to the ClawHavoc campaign that infiltrated 1,200+ malicious skills into the OpenClaw marketplace. Introduces Dolev-Yao adaptation for skill lifecycle security with verified guarantees.

entry.title: Transformers Remember First, Forget Last: Dual-Process Interference in LLMs

author.name: Sourav Chattaraj, Kanak Raj

entry.summary: Studies memory interference in LLMs using cognitive psychology paradigms across 39 models, finding that proactive interference universally dominates retroactive interference (opposite of humans), and that RI and PI reflect separate memory mechanisms.

entry.title: Atomicity for Agents: Exposing, Exploiting, and Mitigating TOCTOU Vulnerabilities in Browser-Use Agents

author.name: Linxi Jiang, Zhijie Liu, Haotian Luo, Zhiqiang Lin

entry.summary: Identifies TOCTOU (time-of-check to time-of-use) vulnerabilities in browser-use AI agents where web pages change between planning and execution, causing agents to act on stale information. Evaluates 10 popular open-source agents with a comprehensive benchmark.

entry.title: Defensive Refusal Bias: How Safety Alignment Fails Cyber Defenders

author.name: David Campbell, Neil Kale, Udari Madhushani Sehwag, Bert Herring, Nick Price, Dan Borges, Alex Levinson, Christina Q Knight

entry.summary: Studies Defensive Refusal Bias - safety-tuned LLMs refusing legitimate defensive cybersecurity tasks at 2.72x the rate of neutral requests. Based on 2,390 real-world examples from NCCDC competition.

entry.title: CharacterFlywheel: Scaling Iterative Improvement of Engaging and Steerable LLMs in Production

author.name: Yixin Nie, Lin Guan, Zhongyao Ma, Anchit Gupta, Yipin Zhou, Xiao Li, Zhengping Zhou, Raymond Zeng, Gelin Zhou, Shigan Chu, Ajay Thampi, Wancen Mu, Nathan Shuster, Ketong Wang, Lin Chen, Jason Brewer, Derek Hao Hu, Alexander McCauley, Jason Weston, Sem Park, Na Zhang, Kevin Tang

entry.summary: Presents CharacterFlywheel, Meta's iterative process for improving LLMs in production social chat applications across Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger, showing consistent engagement improvements across 15 model generations from July 2024 to April 2025.

entry.title: Demystifying Group Relative Policy Optimization: Its Policy Gradient is a U-Statistic

author.name: Hongyi Zhou, Kai Ye, Erhan Xu, Jin Zhu, Shijin Gong, Chengchun Shi

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical framework for understanding GRPO (used in DeepSeek-R1) through U-statistics, deriving MSE bounds, finite-sample error bounds, and showing asymptotic equivalence to an oracle policy gradient estimator.

entry.title: Scalable Multi-Task Low-Rank Model Adaptation

author.name: Zichen Tian, Antoine Ledent, Qianru Sun

entry.summary: Addresses catastrophic performance degradation when scaling multi-task LoRA to many tasks. Identifies parameter and representation misalignment as root causes and proposes solutions based on spectral value-aware regularization and improved routing.

entry.title: Expanding LLM Agent Boundaries with Strategy-Guided Exploration

author.name: Andrew Szot, Michael Kirchhof, Omar Attia, Alexander Toshev

entry.summary: Strategy-Guided Exploration (SGE) leverages LLMs' planning abilities to shift RL exploration from low-level actions to higher-level language strategies, generating natural-language strategies before executing action sequences.

entry.title: LongRLVR: Long-Context Reinforcement Learning Requires Verifiable Context Rewards

author.name: Guanzheng Chen, Michael Qizhe Shieh, Lidong Bing

entry.summary: Identifies that RLVR fails in long-context scenarios due to vanishing gradients for context grounding, proves this formally, and proposes verifiable context rewards to guide evidence identification in long-context RL training.

entry.title: Secretary of War Tweets That Anthropic is Now a Supply Chain Risk

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's detailed analysis of the escalating conflict between Secretary of War Hegseth and Anthropic, where Anthropic has been declared a 'supply chain risk' after contract cancellation, with potential implications for the company's survival and broader AI ecosystem. Covers the geopolitical dynamics, corruption concerns, and potential consequences for AI safety.

entry.title: Constitutional Black-Box Monitoring for Scheming in LLM Agents

author.name: Simon Storf, Rich Barton-Cooper, James Peters-Gill, Marius Hobbhahn

entry.summary: Studies constitutional black-box monitors for detecting scheming in LLM agents, using prompted classifiers on externally observable inputs/outputs optimized on synthetic data from behavior specifications.

entry.title: Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models

author.name: Adel Javanmard, Baharan Mirzasoleiman, Vahab Mirrokni

entry.summary: Theoretically analyzes why pretraining and RL require large datasets while SFT excels on smaller ones, and what defines high-quality SFT data. Reveals synergistic effects between pre-training and post-training for transformers.

entry.title: Efficient RLVR Training via Weighted Mutual Information Data Selection

author.name: Xinyu Zhou, Boyu Zhu, Haotian Zhang, Huiming Wang, Zhijiang Guo

entry.summary: InSight proposes an information-guided data selection method for RL training of LLMs using weighted mutual information, moving beyond difficulty-based heuristics by incorporating epistemic uncertainty from limited evidence.

entry.title: If ‘bad guys’ don't pause, do you?

author.name: Remmelt

entry.summary: Presents five design principles for building evaluation environments that help distinguish between benign and malign model motivations (e.g., scheming vs. confusion). Developed during MATS 9.0 under Neel Nanda's guidance, drawing on experience building 20+ environments. Emphasizes ruling out confounds like ambiguity and instruction conflict.

entry.title: Silo-Bench: A Scalable Environment for Evaluating Distributed Coordination in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Yuzhe Zhang, Feiran Liu, Yi Shan, Xinyi Huang, Xin Yang, Yueqi Zhu, Xuxin Cheng, Cao Liu, Ke Zeng, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Wenyuan Jiang

entry.summary: Silo-Bench evaluates distributed coordination in multi-agent LLM systems across 30 algorithmic tasks, revealing a 'Communication-Reasoning Gap' where agents coordinate well but fail to synthesize distributed information into correct answers.

entry.title: Causal Circuit Tracing Reveals Distinct Computational Architectures in Single-Cell Foundation Models: Inhibitory Dominance, Biological Coherence, and Cross-Model Convergence

author.name: Ihor Kendiukhov

entry.summary: Introduces causal circuit tracing for biological foundation models (Geneformer, scGPT) by ablating sparse autoencoder features and measuring downstream responses. Finds ~53% biological coherence and 65-89% inhibitory dominance across models.

entry.title: Draft-Thinking: Learning Efficient Reasoning in Long Chain-of-Thought LLMs

author.name: Jie Cao, Tianwei Lin, Zhenxuan Fan, Bo Yuan, Ziyuan Zhao, Rolan Yan, Wenqiao Zhang, Siliang Tang

entry.summary: Proposes Draft-Thinking, which trains models to first generate concise draft-style reasoning before producing full chain-of-thought, addressing the overthinking problem in large reasoning models while preserving reasoning capability.

entry.title: Learning Structured Reasoning via Tractable Trajectory Control

author.name: Po-Nien Kung, Zhen Yang, Jeffrey Luo, Cheng-Fu Yang, Haikang Deng, Zi-Yi Dou, Yinfei Yang, Nanyun Peng, Zhe Gan, Kai-Wei Chang

entry.summary: Proposes Ctrl-R, a framework for learning structured reasoning in LLMs by systematically discovering and reinforcing diverse reasoning patterns (like verification and backtracking) through tractable trajectory control during RL training.

entry.title: Dr. Seg: Revisiting GRPO Training for Visual Large Language Models through Perception-Oriented Design

author.name: Haoxiang Sun, Tao Wang, Chenwei Tang, Li Yuan, Jiancheng Lv

entry.summary: Dr. Seg challenges the assumption that GRPO training paradigms from language reasoning transfer seamlessly to visual perception tasks. Identifies two overlooked factors: need for broader output space and importance of perception-specific reward design for visual LLMs.

entry.title: Hidden in the Metadata: Stealth Poisoning Attacks on Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Kennedy Edemacu, Mohammad Mahdi Shokri

entry.summary: MM-MEPA demonstrates a stealth poisoning attack on multimodal RAG systems by manipulating only metadata of image-text entries while leaving visual content unaltered, successfully steering retrieval and model responses.

entry.title: CIRCUS: Circuit Consensus under Uncertainty via Stability Ensembles

author.name: Swapnil Parekh

entry.summary: CIRCUS reframes mechanistic circuit discovery as an uncertainty quantification problem, building ensembles over analyst choices (pruning thresholds, feature dictionaries) to extract robust consensus circuits with stability scores.

entry.title: Theory of Code Space: Do Code Agents Understand Software Architecture?

author.name: Grigory Sapunov

entry.summary: Theory of Code Space (ToCS) benchmarks whether AI code agents can build and maintain coherent architectural beliefs about multi-file codebases, testing structured understanding of module dependencies and design intent under partial observability.

entry.title: LLM Self-Explanations Fail Semantic Invariance

author.name: Stefan Szeider

entry.summary: Demonstrates that LLM self-explanations fail semantic invariance testing - a relief-framed tool that changes nothing about a task still produces significant reductions in self-reported aversiveness across four frontier models.

entry.title: When does Chain-of-Thought Help: A Markovian Perspective

author.name: Zihan Wang, Yijun Dong, Qi Lei

entry.summary: Analyzes when Chain-of-Thought prompting helps by modeling reasoning as a Markov chain, identifying 'transition alignment' (whether instances share a common step-wise transition kernel) as the key determinant of CoT effectiveness.

entry.title: Training Dynamics of Softmax Self-Attention: Fast Global Convergence via Preconditioning

author.name: Gautam Goel, Mahdi Soltanolkotabi, Peter Bartlett

entry.summary: Studies training dynamics of gradient descent in softmax self-attention for linear regression, showing a structure-aware gradient descent variant can converge globally at geometric rate. Connects the problem to nonconvex matrix factorization.

entry.title: Tool Verification for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ruotong Liao, Nikolai R\"ohrich, Xiaohan Wang, Yuhui Zhang, Yasaman Samadzadeh, Volker Tresp, Serena Yeung-Levy

entry.summary: Proposes T³RL, which introduces tool verification into test-time reinforcement learning to combat incorrect mode collapse. Uses external tools (e.g., code execution) to upweight verified rollouts in a verification-aware voting mechanism for more reliable pseudo-labels.

entry.title: Stepwise Penalization for Length-Efficient Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Xintong Li, Sha Li, Rongmei Lin, Hongye Jin, Linwei Li, Hejie Cui, Sarah Zhang, Chia-Yuan Chang, Kewei Cheng, Besnik Fetahu, Priyanka Nigam, Jingbo Shang, Bing Yin

entry.summary: SWAP proposes step-wise adaptive penalization for chain-of-thought reasoning, applying fine-grained length reduction at the step level during RL training rather than trajectory-level penalties, distinguishing essential from redundant reasoning steps.

entry.title: One-Token Verification for Reasoning Correctness Estimation

author.name: Zhan Zhuang, Xiequn Wang, Zebin Chen, Feiyang Ye, Ying Wei, Kede Ma, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: One-Token Verification (OTV) estimates reasoning correctness of LLM outputs using a single verification token, enabling efficient best-of-N selection without expensive multi-sample decoding or full verification.

entry.title: One Operator to Rule Them All? On Boundary-Indexed Operator Families in Neural PDE Solvers

author.name: Lennon J. Shikhman

entry.summary: Argues that standard neural PDE solvers implicitly learn boundary-indexed families of operators rather than single operators when boundary conditions vary. Formalizes this as conditional risk minimization and proves non-identifiability outside training boundary distributions.

entry.title: Conformal Policy Control

author.name: Drew Prinster, Clara Fannjiang, Ji Won Park, Kyunghyun Cho, Anqi Liu, Suchi Saria, Samuel Stanton

entry.summary: Introduces Conformal Policy Control, which uses conformal calibration on data from a safe reference policy to regulate how aggressively a new untested policy can act, providing provable risk tolerance guarantees without assumptions about model class correctness.

entry.title: Steering Away from Memorization: Reachability-Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Text-to-Image Diffusion

author.name: Sathwik Karnik, Juyeop Kim, Sanmi Koyejo, Jong-Seok Lee, Somil Bansal

entry.summary: RADS models diffusion denoising as a dynamical system and uses reachability analysis to identify states that lead to memorized outputs, then formulates memorization mitigation as constrained RL. Prevents memorization while preserving generation quality.

entry.title: A Comprehensive Evaluation of LLM Unlearning Robustness under Multi-Turn Interaction

author.name: Ruihao Pan, Suhang Wang

entry.summary: Studies LLM unlearning robustness under multi-turn interaction, finding that knowledge appearing forgotten in static evaluation can be recovered through self-correction and dialogue-conditioned querying.

entry.title: Turning Black Box into White Box: Dataset Distillation Leaks

author.name: Huajie Chen, Tianqing Zhu, Yuchen Zhong, Yang Zhang, Shang Wang, Feng He, Lefeng Zhang, Jialiang Shen, Minghao Wang, Wanlei Zhou

entry.summary: Demonstrates that dataset distillation can cause severe privacy leakage because synthetic datasets implicitly encode model weight trajectories. The Information Revelation Attack accurately predicts distillation algorithms and model architectures.

entry.title: Learning from Synthetic Data Improves Multi-hop Reasoning

author.name: Anmol Kabra, Yilun Yin, Albert Gong, Kamil\.e Stankevi\v{c}i\=ut\.e, Dongyoung Go, Johann Lee, Katie Z. Luo, Carla P. Gomes, Kilian Q. Weinberger

entry.summary: Shows that RL fine-tuning on rule-generated synthetic data significantly improves multi-hop reasoning in LLMs, offering a cheaper alternative to human annotations, LLM-generated data, or LLM-based verifiers.

entry.title: TopoCurate:Modeling Interaction Topology for Tool-Use Agent Training

author.name: Jinluan Yang, Yuxin Liu, Zhengyu Chen, Chengcheng Han, Yueqing Sun, Qi Gu, Hui Su, Xunliang Cai, Fei Wu, Kun Kuang

entry.summary: TopoCurate proposes an interaction-aware framework for training tool-use agents that uses semantic quotient topology to analyze multi-trial rollouts, going beyond simple outcome-based filtering for SFT and RL data selection.

entry.title: Never Saddle for Reparameterized Steepest Descent as Mirror Flow

author.name: Tom Jacobs, Chao Zhou, Rebekka Burkholz

entry.summary: Analyzes steepest descent methods (including sign descent/Adam) through a 'steepest mirror flows' framework, showing that steeper descent facilitates saddle-point escape and feature learning in diagonal networks.

entry.title: The Hidden Costs of Domain Fine-Tuning: Pii-Bearing Data Degrades Safety and Increases Leakage

author.name: Jayesh Choudhari, Piyush Kumar Singh

entry.summary: Studies how domain fine-tuning with PII-bearing data degrades safety alignment and increases privacy leakage in small instruction-tuned LLMs, even when the target domain is benign.

entry.title: The Lattice Representation Hypothesis of Large Language Models

author.name: Bo Xiong

entry.summary: Proposes the Lattice Representation Hypothesis: LLM embeddings encode concept lattices via half-space intersections, unifying the Linear Representation Hypothesis with Formal Concept Analysis. Experiments on WordNet hierarchies provide evidence.

entry.title: Beyond Length Scaling: Synergizing Breadth and Depth for Generative Reward Models

author.name: Qiyuan Zhang, Yufei Wang, Tianhe Wu, Can Xu, Qingfeng Sun, Kai Zheng, Xue Liu, Chen Ma

entry.summary: Proposes Mix-GRM, a framework that structures Chain-of-Thought reasoning in Generative Reward Models into Breadth-CoT (multi-dimensional principle coverage) and Depth-CoT (substantive judgment). Uses SFT and RLVR to optimize these complementary reasoning mechanisms.

entry.title: Maximizing the Spectral Energy Gain in Sub-1-Bit LLMs via Latent Geometry Alignment

author.name: Banseok Lee, Youngmin Kim

entry.summary: Proposes LittleBit-2 for sub-1-bit LLM compression, identifying that standard singular vectors have high coherence (worst-case for binary quantization) and using Internal Latent Rotation and Joint-ITQ as geometric preconditioners with zero inference overhead.

entry.title: TinyVLM: Zero-Shot Object Detection on Microcontrollers via Vision-Language Distillation with Matryoshka Embeddings

author.name: Bibin Wilson

entry.summary: TinyVLM enables zero-shot object detection on microcontrollers with <1MB memory by decoupling visual inference from text encoding, using Matryoshka distillation for flexible accuracy-memory tradeoffs. First framework for zero-shot detection on MCUs.

entry.title: VisRef: Visual Refocusing while Thinking Improves Test-Time Scaling in Multi-Modal Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Soumya Suvra Ghosal, Youngeun Kim, Zhuowei Li, Ritwick Chaudhry, Linghan Xu, Hongjing Zhang, Jakub Zablocki, Yifan Xing, Qin Zhang

entry.summary: VisRef proposes visual refocusing during extended reasoning in multimodal LRMs, addressing the problem where models progressively lose attention to visual tokens during long reasoning chains. Training-free approach that improves test-time scaling.

entry.title: MIDAS: Multi-Image Dispersion and Semantic Reconstruction for Jailbreaking MLLMs

author.name: Yilian Liu, Xiaojun Jia, Guoshun Nan, Jiuyang Lyu, Zhican Chen, Tao Guan, Shuyuan Luo, Zhongyi Zhai, Yang Liu

entry.summary: MIDAS proposes a multi-image jailbreak attack on multimodal LLMs that disperses harmful content across multiple images to extend reasoning paths and circumvent safety mechanisms, targeting even strongly aligned commercial models.

entry.title: Thoth: Mid-Training Bridges LLMs to Time Series Understanding

author.name: Jiafeng Lin, Yuxuan Wang, Jialong Wu, Huakun Luo, Zhongyi Pei, Jianmin Wang

entry.summary: Thoth introduces the first family of mid-trained LLMs with general-purpose time series understanding, using a specialized mid-training corpus (Book-of-Thoth) for task-agnostic alignment between time series and language.

entry.title: Token-level Data Selection for Safe LLM Fine-tuning

author.name: Yanping Li, Zhening Liu, Zijian Li, Zehong Lin, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: TOSS proposes token-level data selection for safe LLM fine-tuning by quantifying the safety risk of each token and selectively filtering harmful tokens while preserving utility. This is finer-grained than existing sample-level approaches.

entry.title: Provable and Practical In-Context Policy Optimization for Self-Improvement

author.name: Tianrun Yu, Yuxiao Yang, Zhaoyang Wang, Kaixiang Zhao, Porter Jenkins, Xuchao Zhang, Chetan Bansal, Huaxiu Yao, Weitong Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces In-Context Policy Optimization (ICPO), showing that with proper pretraining, models can optimize policies at test time using self-assessed rewards without parameter modification. Proposes ME-ICPO as a practical algorithm.

entry.title: LFPO: Likelihood-Free Policy Optimization for Masked Diffusion Models

author.name: Chenxing Wei, Jiazhen Kang, Hong Wang, Jianqing Zhang, Hao Jiang, Xiaolong Xu, Ningyuan Sun, Ying He, F. Richard Yu, Yao Shu, Bo Jiang

entry.summary: LFPO proposes Likelihood-Free Policy Optimization for masked diffusion models, formulating alignment as geometric velocity rectification to bypass intractable likelihood computation for RLVR.

entry.title: Real Money, Fake Models: Deceptive Model Claims in Shadow APIs

author.name: Yage Zhang, Yukun Jiang, Zeyuan Chen, Michael Backes, Xinyue Shen, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: Conducts the first systematic audit of 'shadow APIs'—third-party services claiming to provide access to frontier LLMs like GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5. Identifies 17 shadow APIs and investigates whether they deliver outputs consistent with official APIs.

entry.title: Subliminal Signals in Preference Labels

author.name: Isotta Magistrali, Fr\'ed\'eric Berdoz, Sam Dauncey, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: Demonstrates that preference labels in LLM-as-a-judge frameworks can function as a covert communication channel, where a biased judge can transmit unintended behavioral traits through preference assignments that strengthen across iterative alignment rounds.

entry.title: 3BASiL: An Algorithmic Framework for Sparse plus Low-Rank Compression of LLMs

author.name: Mehdi Makni, Xiang Meng, Rahul Mazumder

entry.summary: 3BASiL proposes an efficient one-shot post-training method for decomposing LLM weights into sparse plus low-rank matrices using a novel 3-Block ADMM algorithm. The approach aims to reduce performance degradation compared to existing sparse+low-rank compression methods.

entry.title: D3LM: A Discrete DNA Diffusion Language Model for Bidirectional DNA Understanding and Generation

author.name: Zhao Yang, Hengchang Liu, Chuan Cao, Bing Su

entry.summary: D3LM unifies bidirectional DNA representation learning and generation through masked diffusion, reformulating the Nucleotide Transformer v2 training objective as masked diffusion in discrete DNA space.

entry.title: LLaDA-o: An Effective and Length-Adaptive Omni Diffusion Model

author.name: Zebin You, Xiaolu Zhang, Jun Zhou, Chongxuan Li, Ji-Rong Wen

entry.summary: LLaDA-o is an omni diffusion model combining discrete masked diffusion for text understanding and continuous diffusion for visual generation through a shared attention backbone, with a length-adaptive decoding strategy.

entry.title: Embracing Anisotropy: Turning Massive Activations into Interpretable Control Knobs for Large Language Models

author.name: Youngji Roh, Hyunjin Cho, Jaehyung Kim

entry.summary: Reframes the phenomenon of massive activations in LLMs (where a few feature dimensions have extremely large magnitudes) as interpretable functional units rather than artifacts. Proposes training-free identification of domain-critical dimensions that serve as semantic detectors.

entry.title: How RL Unlocks the Aha Moment in Geometric Interleaved Reasoning

author.name: Xiangxiang Zhang, Caijun Jia, Siyuan Li, Dingyu He, Xiya Xiong, Zheng Sun, Honghao He, Yuchen Wu, Bihui Yu, Linzhuang Sun, Cheng Tan, Jingxuan Wei

entry.summary: Discovers that SFT on interleaved plot-solution data degrades geometric reasoning performance, and proposes RL-based training that enables models to genuinely learn interleaved diagram construction with logical deduction (aha moment).

entry.title: Learning to Draft: Adaptive Speculative Decoding with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jiebin Zhang, Zhenghan Yu, Liang Wang, Nan Yang, Eugene J. Yu, Zheng Li, Yifan Song, Dawei Zhu, Xingxing Zhang, Furu Wei, Sujian Li

entry.summary: Introduces Learning to Draft (LTD), using reinforcement learning to optimize speculative decoding by directly maximizing throughput of each draft-and-verify cycle, rather than proxy metrics like acceptance length.

entry.title: Infinite Self-Attention

author.name: Giorgio Roffo

entry.summary: Introduces Infinite Self-Attention (InfSA), a spectral reformulation linking self-attention to graph centrality measures (Katz, PageRank) via Neumann series over attention matrices, with a linear-time variant.

entry.title: Learning Physics from Pretrained Video Models: A Multimodal Continuous and Sequential World Interaction Models for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zijian Song, Qichang Li, Sihan Qin, Yuhao Chen, Tianshui Chen, Liang Lin, Guangrun Wang

entry.summary: Introduces PhysGen, which uses pretrained autoregressive video generation models as physics simulators for robotic manipulation. Creates a multimodal continuous representation that unifies video and action into shared physical tokens, bridging discrete video generation and continuous robot control.

entry.title: Personalization Increases Affective Alignment but Has Role-Dependent Effects on Epistemic Independence in LLMs

author.name: Sean W. Kelley, Christoph Riedl

entry.summary: Evaluates how personalization affects LLM sycophancy across nine frontier models and five benchmarks. Finds personalization increases affective alignment (emotional validation) but has role-dependent effects on epistemic independence.

entry.title: Summer-22B: A Systematic Approach to Dataset Engineering and Training at Scale for Video Foundation Model

author.name: Simo Ryu, Chunghwan Han

entry.summary: Documents the training of Summer-22B, a video foundation model, sharing lessons on dataset engineering, μP parameterization, and hypersphere-constrained optimization across 50M video clips. Key finding: dataset engineering mattered more than architectural choices.

entry.title: General Proximal Flow Networks

author.name: Alexander Strunk, Roland Assam

entry.summary: General Proximal Flow Networks (GPFNs) generalize Bayesian Flow Networks by replacing Bayesian posterior updates with arbitrary divergence functions (e.g., Wasserstein), creating a unified proximal-operator framework for generative modeling.

entry.title: Knowledge without Wisdom: Measuring Misalignment between LLMs and Intended Impact

author.name: Michael Hardy, Yunsung Kim

entry.summary: Examines misalignment between LLM benchmark performance and downstream task validity in education, finding that LLM behaviors correlate more with each other than with human experts, and multi-model ensembles can exacerbate misalignment with learning outcomes.

entry.title: Self-Anchoring Calibration Drift in Large Language Models: How Multi-Turn Conversations Reshape Model Confidence

author.name: Harshavardhan

entry.summary: Introduces Self-Anchoring Calibration Drift (SACD), studying how LLMs systematically change expressed confidence when building on their own outputs in multi-turn conversations. Compares Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.2 across 150 questions.

entry.title: MetaState: Persistent Working Memory for Discrete Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Kejing Xia, Mingzhe Li, Lixuan Wei, Zhenbang Du, Xiangchi Yuan, Qirui Jin, Wenke Lee

entry.summary: MetaState adds persistent working memory to discrete diffusion language models through a lightweight recurrent augmentation, addressing the 'Information Island' problem where intermediate representations are discarded between denoising steps.

entry.title: Surgical Post-Training: Cutting Errors, Keeping Knowledge

author.name: Wenye Lin, Kai Han

entry.summary: Surgical Post-Training (SPoT) reveals that DPO's reward estimate provides implicit regularization against forgetting, then proposes a paradigm that surgically corrects erroneous reasoning steps via minimal edits.

entry.title: Agentic Code Reasoning

author.name: Shubham Ugare, Satish Chandra

entry.summary: Introduces 'semi-formal reasoning' for LLM agents to explore codebases without execution—requiring explicit premises, execution path tracing, and formal conclusions. Shows improvements in patch equivalence verification, fault localization, and code QA.

entry.title: SageBwd: A Trainable Low-bit Attention

author.name: Jintao Zhang, Marco Chen, Haoxu Wang, Kai Jiang, Ion Stoica, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Jianfei Chen, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces SageBwd, showing that INT8 attention can match full-precision attention during pretraining when QK-norm is applied. Identifies key insights about quantization-aware training stability.

entry.title: Spectral Condition for $\mu$P under Width-Depth Scaling

author.name: Chenyu Zheng, Rongzhen Wang, Xinyu Zhang, Chongxuan Li

entry.summary: Develops a spectral framework for maximal update parameterization (μP) under joint width-depth scaling for residual networks, providing a unified spectral condition that characterizes how weight and residual branch norms should scale.

entry.title: I Can't Believe It's Not Robust: Catastrophic Collapse of Safety Classifiers under Embedding Drift

author.name: Subramanyam Sahoo, Vinija Jain, Divya Chaudhary, Aman Chadha

entry.summary: Shows that safety classifiers trained on frozen embeddings catastrophically fail under small embedding perturbations (σ=0.02 causes drop from 85% to 50% ROC-AUC), with dangerous silent failures where 72% of misclassifications occur with high confidence.

entry.title: Autoregressive Synthesis of Sparse and Semi-Structured Mixed-Type Data

author.name: Thomas R\"uckstie{\ss}, Robin Vujanic

entry.summary: Origami is an autoregressive transformer-based architecture for generating synthetic data in sparse, semi-structured formats like JSON, handling nested objects and variable-length arrays natively rather than requiring flattening to tabular form.

entry.title: SEAR: Sample Efficient Action Chunking Reinforcement Learning

author.name: C. F. Maximilian Nagy, Onur Celik, Emiliyan Gospodinov, Florian Seligmann, Weiran Liao, Aryan Kaushik, Gerhard Neumann

entry.summary: SEAR introduces an online RL algorithm for action chunking that exploits temporal structure with a receding horizon, combining benefits of small and large chunk sizes for long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: GRIP: Geometric Refinement and Adaptive Information Potential for Data Efficiency

author.name: Changhao Wang, Jiaolong Yang, Xinhao Yao, Yunfei Yu, Peng Jiao, Lu Yu, Junpeng Fang, Riccardo Cantoro, Qing Cui, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: GRIP is a data selection framework for LLM training that models the corpus as an information-dense geometric space, using a Rapid Adaptation Probe to allocate sampling budgets to regions with highest representation deficits.

entry.title: Truth as a Trajectory: What Internal Representations Reveal About Large Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Hamed Damirchi, Ignacio Meza De la Jara, Ehsan Abbasnejad, Afshar Shamsi, Zhen Zhang, Javen Shi

entry.summary: Truth as a Trajectory (TaT) models LLM inference as layer-wise geometric displacement trajectories rather than static hidden states, discovering geometric invariants that distinguish valid from invalid reasoning.

entry.title: RLAR: An Agentic Reward System for Multi-task Reinforcement Learning on Large Language Models

author.name: Andrew Zhuoer Feng, Cunxiang Wang, Bosi Wen, Yidong Wang, Yu Luo, Hongning Wang, Minlie Huang

entry.summary: Presents RLAR, an agent-driven reward framework for RL alignment that dynamically assigns tailored reward functions by retrieving reward models from the internet and synthesizing programmatic verifiers through code generation.

entry.title: KVSlimmer: Theoretical Insights and Practical Optimizations for Asymmetric KV Merging

author.name: Lianjun Liu, Hongli An, Weiqi Yan, Xin Du, Shengchuan Zhang, Huazhong Liu, Yunshan Zhong

entry.summary: Establishes theoretical framework for KV cache asymmetry through spectral energy distribution analysis, showing Query/Key weights induce feature homogeneity while Value weights preserve heterogeneity. Proposes KVSlimmer for efficient asymmetric KV merging.

entry.title: AdaPonderLM: Gated Pondering Language Models with Token-Wise Adaptive Depth

author.name: Shixiang Song, He Li, Zitong Wang, Boyi Zeng, Feichen Song, Yixuan Wang, Zhiqin John Xu, Ziwei He, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: Proposes AdaPonderLM, a self-supervised recurrent language model that learns token-wise adaptive early exiting during pretraining using monotonic halting masks and KV reuse for efficient test-time compute allocation.

entry.title: CASCADE: Cross-scale Advective Super-resolution with Climate Assimilation and Downscaling Evolution

author.name: Alexander Kovalenko

entry.summary: CASCADE reframes spatiotemporal super-resolution of geophysical fields as an explicit transport process across scales, using advection to maintain physical consistency rather than hallucinating pixel-level detail.

entry.title: The Synthetic Web: Adversarially-Curated Mini-Internets for Diagnosing Epistemic Weaknesses of Language Agents

author.name: Shrey Shah, Levent Ozgur

entry.summary: Introduces Synthetic Web Benchmark - procedurally generated mini-internets with adversarial content to test language agents' robustness to misleading information appearing prominently in search results.

entry.title: Tracking Capabilities for Safer Agents

author.name: Martin Odersky, Yaoyu Zhao, Yichen Xu, Oliver Bra\v{c}evac, Cao Nguyen Pham

entry.summary: Proposes using Scala 3's capture checking type system as a safety harness for AI agents, where capabilities tracked statically provide fine-grained control over agent effects like tool access and information flow.

entry.title: Alien Science: Sampling Coherent but Cognitively Unavailable Research Directions from Idea Atoms

author.name: Alejandro H. Artiles, Martin Weiss, Levin Brinkmann, Anirudh Goyal, Nasim Rahaman

entry.summary: Formalizes 'cognitive availability' in research idea generation and introduces a pipeline to decompose papers into idea atoms, then sample coherent but non-obvious research directions using coherence and availability models.

entry.title: FT-Dojo: Towards Autonomous LLM Fine-Tuning with Language Agents

author.name: Qizheng Li, Yifei Zhang, Xiao Yang, Xu Yang, Zhuo Wang, Weiqing Liu, Jiang Bian

entry.summary: Introduces FT-Dojo, the first system framing end-to-end LLM fine-tuning as an autonomous agent task, where agents must navigate data curation, training configuration, and iterative refinement. Provides a benchmark for this challenging open-ended problem.

entry.title: CARE: Confounder-Aware Aggregation for Reliable LLM Evaluation

author.name: Jitian Zhao, Changho Shin, Tzu-Heng Huang, Satya Sai Srinath Namburi GNVV, Frederic Sala

entry.summary: Introduces CARE, a confounder-aware aggregation framework for LLM-as-judge ensembles that explicitly models correlated errors from shared latent confounders (verbosity, style) rather than assuming judge independence.

entry.title: Expert Divergence Learning for MoE-based Language Models

author.name: Jiaang Li, Haibin Chen, Langming Liu, Yujin Yuan, Yadao Wang, Yizhen Zhang, Chengting Yu, Xin Tong, Weidong Zhang, Shilei Liu, Wenbo Su, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces Expert Divergence Learning, a pre-training strategy for MoE language models that uses label-driven auxiliary loss to maximize Jensen-Shannon Divergence between expert routing distributions across different data domains, combating expert homogenization.

entry.title: You Don't Need All That Attention: Surgical Memorization Mitigation in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Kairan Zhao, Eleni Triantafillou, Peter Triantafillou

entry.summary: GUARD introduces a framework for mitigating memorization in text-to-image diffusion models by guiding generation away from training images using attractive-repulsive dynamics during denoising, without hurting image quality.

entry.title: Exploring the AI Obedience: Why is Generating a Pure Color Image Harder than CyberPunk?

author.name: Hongyu Li, Kuan Liu, Yuan Chen, Juntao Hu, Huimin Lu, Guanjie Chen, Xue Liu, Guangming Lu, Hong Huang

entry.summary: Formalizes 'AI Obedience' - the ability of generative models to follow precise instructions - revealing a 'Paradox of Simplicity' where models can generate complex scenes but fail at simple deterministic tasks like pure color images. Introduces VIOLIN benchmark.

entry.title: Embedding Morphology into Transformers for Cross-Robot Policy Learning

author.name: Kei Suzuki, Jing Liu, Ye Wang, Chiori Hori, Matthew Brand, Diego Romeres, Toshiaki Koike-Akino

entry.summary: Proposes embodiment-aware transformer policies for cross-robot learning with kinematic tokens, topology-aware attention bias, and morphology-conditioned adapters. Enables single policy to work across different robot embodiments.

entry.title: Verifier-Bound Communication for LLM Agents: Certified Bounds on Covert Signaling

author.name: Om Tailor

entry.summary: CLBC protocol for verifier-bound communication between LLM agents, proving upper bounds on transcript leakage and preventing covert signaling between colluding agents.

entry.title: Are LLMs Reliable Code Reviewers? Systematic Overcorrection in Requirement Conformance Judgement

author.name: Haolin Jin, Huaming Chen

entry.summary: Reveals systematic overcorrection bias in LLMs used for code review—models frequently misclassify correct code as non-compliant with requirements, suggesting LLMs are unreliable for requirement conformance verification.

entry.title: A Gauge Theory of Superposition: Toward a Sheaf-Theoretic Atlas of Neural Representations

author.name: Hossein Javidnia

entry.summary: Develops a gauge-theoretic framework using sheaf theory for understanding superposition in LLMs, replacing single-global-dictionary approaches with local semantic charts and identifying three measurable obstructions to interpretability.

entry.title: CHIMERA: Compact Synthetic Data for Generalizable LLM Reasoning

author.name: Xinyu Zhu, Yihao Feng, Yanchao Sun, Xianzhi Du, Pingzhi Li, Olli Saarikivi, Yun Zhu, Yu Meng

entry.summary: CHIMERA generates compact synthetic reasoning data addressing the cold-start problem, limited domain coverage, and annotation bottleneck for training LLM reasoning capabilities across scientific disciplines beyond math.

entry.title: Hide&Seek: Remove Image Watermarks with Negligible Cost via Pixel-wise Reconstruction

author.name: Huajie Chen, Tianqing Zhu, Hailin Yang, Yuchen Zhong, Yang Zhang, Hui Sun, Heng Xu, Zuobin Ying, Lihua Yin, Wanlei Zhou

entry.summary: HIDE&SEEK demonstrates versatile and cost-effective attacks that reliably remove embedded watermarks from machine-generated images while preserving visual quality, challenging the robustness of watermarking defenses.

entry.title: Unified Vision-Language Modeling via Concept Space Alignment

author.name: Yifu Qiu, Paul-Ambroise Duquenne, Holger Schwenk

entry.summary: V-SONAR extends the SONAR text embedding space (1500 languages) to vision, achieving competitive text-to-video retrieval and state-of-the-art video captioning. Demonstrates cross-lingual transfer for video understanding.

entry.title: VisNec: Measuring and Leveraging Visual Necessity for Multimodal Instruction Tuning

author.name: Mingkang Dong, Hongyi Cai, Jie Li, Sifan Zhou, Bin Ren, Kunyu Peng, Yuqian Fu

entry.summary: VisNec introduces a Visual Necessity Score that measures the marginal contribution of visual input during multimodal instruction tuning, identifying vision-critical vs. redundant training samples to improve data quality.

entry.title: Attention Smoothing Is All You Need For Unlearning

author.name: Saleh Zare Zade, Xiangyu Zhou, Sijia Liu, Dongxiao Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes Attention Smoothing Unlearning (ASU) which casts LLM unlearning as self-distillation from a forget-teacher derived from the model's own attention, flattening attention distributions to suppress memorized associations.

entry.title: GAC: Stabilizing Asynchronous RL Training for LLMs via Gradient Alignment Control

author.name: Haofeng Xu, Junwei Su, Yukun Tian, Lansong Diao, Zhengping Qian, Chuan Wu

entry.summary: GAC identifies and addresses training instability in asynchronous RL for LLMs caused by high cosine similarity between consecutive gradients, proposing gradient alignment control for stabilization.

entry.title: Measuring What VLMs Don't Say: Validation Metrics Hide Clinical Terminology Erasure in Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Aditya Parikh, Aasa Feragen, Sneha Das, Stella Frank

entry.summary: Demonstrates that current validation metrics for radiology report generation hide clinical terminology erasure - models achieve high token-overlap scores while generating only repetitive generic text. Introduces Clinical Association Metrics.

entry.title: Reasoning as Gradient: Scaling MLE Agents Beyond Tree Search

author.name: Yifei Zhang, Xu Yang, Xiao Yang, Bowen Xian, Qizheng Li, Shikai Fang, Jingyuan Li, Jian Wang, Mingrui Xu, Weiqing Liu, Jiang Bian

entry.summary: GOME introduces an MLE agent that maps structured diagnostic reasoning to gradient computation, success memory to momentum, and multi-trace execution to distributed optimization, outperforming tree-search approaches.

entry.title: FreeAct: Freeing Activations for LLM Quantization

author.name: Xiaohao Liu, Xiaobo Xia, Manyi Zhang, Ji-Fu Li, Xianzhi Yu, Fei Shen, Xiu Su, See-Kiong Ng, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Already analyzed above.

entry.title: Co-Evolutionary Multi-Modal Alignment via Structured Adversarial Evolution

author.name: Guoxin Shi, Haoyu Wang, Zaihui Yang, Yuxing Wang, Yongzhe Chang

entry.summary: Introduces CEMMA, a co-evolutionary framework for multimodal safety alignment that uses an evolutionary attacker to dynamically generate adversarial prompts while training a defender, moving beyond static adversarial settings.

entry.title: Diagnosing Generalization Failures from Representational Geometry Markers

author.name: Chi-Ning Chou, Artem Kirsanov, Yao-Yuan Yang, SueYeon Chung

entry.summary: Proposes a 'top-down' biomarker-inspired approach to diagnose generalization failures using representational geometry markers, rather than mechanistic interpretability. Identifies system-level measurements that predict model failure.

entry.title: Robometer: Scaling General-Purpose Robotic Reward Models via Trajectory Comparisons

author.name: Anthony Liang, Yigit Korkmaz, Jiahui Zhang, Minyoung Hwang, Abrar Anwar, Sidhant Kaushik, Aditya Shah, Alex S. Huang, Luke Zettlemoyer, Dieter Fox, Yu Xiang, Anqi Li, Andreea Bobu, Abhishek Gupta, Stephen Tu, Erdem Biyik, Jesse Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Robometer, a scalable reward modeling framework for robotics that combines intra-trajectory progress supervision with inter-trajectory preference supervision, enabling learning from both expert and suboptimal demonstrations.

entry.title: Weight Updates as Activation Shifts: A Principled Framework for Steering

author.name: Dyah Adila, John Cooper, Alexander Yun, Avi Trost, Frederic Sala

entry.summary: Establishes first-order equivalence between activation steering and weight-space fine-tuning, deriving principled guidelines for intervention site selection and explaining why certain locations outperform others.

entry.title: Antibody: Strengthening Defense Against Harmful Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models via Attenuating Harmful Gradient Influence

author.name: Quoc Minh Nguyen, Trung Le, Jing Wu, Anh Tuan Bui, Mehrtash Harandi

entry.summary: Introduces Antibody, a defense against harmful fine-tuning attacks on LLMs that regularizes gradient contributions of harmful samples by first ensuring robust safety alignment in flat loss regions, then applying safety-preservation during fine-tuning.

entry.title: Curation Leaks: Membership Inference Attacks against Data Curation for Machine Learning

author.name: Dariush Wahdany (CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security), Matthew Jagielski (Anthropic), Adam Dziedzic (CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security), Franziska Boenisch (CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security)

entry.summary: Introduces novel membership inference attacks against data curation pipelines, showing that even when models are trained only on curated public data, the curation process itself can leak information about private data used for selection.

entry.title: Boosting Entropy with Bell Box Quantization

author.name: Ningfeng Yang, Tor M. Aamodt

entry.summary: BBQ proposes a quantization method that is both information-theoretically optimal and compute-efficient by mapping quantizer outputs to a different domain than inputs. Targets quantization-aware pre-training for edge devices.

entry.title: DGNet: Discrete Green Networks for Data-Efficient Learning of Spatiotemporal PDEs

author.name: Yingjie Tan, Quanming Yao, Yaqing Wang

entry.summary: DGNet incorporates discrete Green's functions as inductive biases in neural PDE solvers to improve data efficiency, particularly for generalizing to unseen source terms in spatiotemporal PDEs.

entry.title: Accelerating Single-Pass SGD for Generalized Linear Prediction

author.name: Qian Chen, Shihong Ding, Cong Fang

entry.summary: Proposes the first algorithm incorporating momentum into single-pass SGD for generalized linear prediction, achieving dual-momentum acceleration with decomposed excess risk bounds for optimization, statistical, and misspecification errors.

entry.title: Strategic Advice in the Age of Personal AI

author.name: Yueyang Liu, Wichinpong Park Sinchaisri

entry.summary: Studies how personal AI assistants change the strategic dynamics of professional advice-giving, showing that advisor performance is non-monotone with adoption level - worst at intermediate adoption rates.

entry.title: Accelerating PDE Surrogates via RL-Guided Mesh Optimization

author.name: Yang Meng, Ruoxi Jiang, Zhuokai Zhao, Chong Liu, Rebecca Willett, Yuxin Chen

entry.summary: RLMesh uses reinforcement learning to adaptively allocate mesh grid points for PDE simulations, focusing numerical resolution on critical regions to train deep surrogate models more efficiently under limited simulation budgets.

entry.title: Grokking as a Phase Transition between Competing Basins: a Singular Learning Theory Approach

author.name: Ben Cullen, Sergio Estan-Ruiz, Riya Danait, Jiayi Li

entry.summary: Interprets grokking as a phase transition between competing solution basins using Singular Learning Theory, deriving closed-form expressions for the local learning coefficient in quadratic networks.

entry.title: SimpleTool: Parallel Decoding for Real-Time LLM Function Calling

author.name: Xiaoxin Shi, Jiaxin Wan, Linkang Dong, Wei Jiang, Yue Liu, Zengfeng Huang

entry.summary: Presents SimpleTool, a parallel decoding method for LLM function calling that compresses low-entropy tokens (4-6x reduction) and enables parallel generation, targeting real-time applications like embodied AI requiring 10Hz+ control frequencies.

entry.title: BLUFF: Benchmarking the Detection of False and Synthetic Content across 58 Low-Resource Languages

author.name: Jason Lucas, Matt Murtagh-White, Adaku Uchendu, Ali Al-Lawati, Michiharu Yamashita, Dominik Macko, Ivan Srba, Robert Moro, Dongwon Lee

entry.summary: Introduces BLUFF, a benchmark for detecting false and synthetic content across 79 languages (59 low-resource) with 202K+ samples, combining human-written fact-checked content and LLM-generated content.

entry.title: PonderLM-3: Adaptive Token-Wise Pondering with Differentiable Masking

author.name: He Li, Feichen Song, Boyi Zeng, Shixiang Song, Zhiqin John Xu, Ziwei He, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: Introduces PonderLM-3, building on PonderLM-2 with differentiable attention masking for token-wise adaptive pondering, making per-token computation allocation learnable with train-inference consistency.

entry.title: Proof-of-Perception: Certified Tool-Using Multimodal Reasoning with Compositional Conformal Guarantees

author.name: Arya Fayyazi, Haleh Akrami

entry.summary: Presents Proof-of-Perception (PoP), a tool-using framework for multimodal reasoning with conformal prediction guarantees at each step, enabling principled accuracy-compute trade-offs with calibrated uncertainty.

entry.title: COMBAT: Conditional World Models for Behavioral Agent Training

author.name: Anmol Agarwal, Pranay Meshram, Sumer Singh, Saurav Suman, Andrew Lapp, Shahbuland Matiana, Louis Castricato, Spencer Frazier

entry.summary: COMBAT trains a 1.2B parameter Diffusion Transformer as a world model on Tekken 3, demonstrating real-time action-conditioned simulation of dynamic opponents. It shows diffusion models can implicitly learn reactive agent behavior.

entry.title: Towards Policy-Adaptive Image Guardrail: Benchmark and Method

author.name: Caiyong Piao, Zhiyuan Yan, Haoming Xu, Yunzhen Zhao, Kaiqing Lin, Feiyang Xu, Shuigeng Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes a policy-adaptive image guardrail benchmark and method, showing existing VLM-based safety methods overfit to seen policies and fail to generalize to new safety policies.

entry.title: When Does RL Help Medical VLMs? Disentangling Vision, SFT, and RL Gains

author.name: Ahmadreza Jeddi, Kimia Shaban, Negin Baghbanzadeh, Natasha Sharan, Abhishek Moturu, Elham Dolatabadi, Babak Taati

entry.summary: Presents a controlled study disentangling when RL helps medical VLMs, finding RL is most effective when models already have non-trivial support (high Pass@K) and primarily sharpens rather than creates new capabilities.

entry.title: RA-Det: Towards Universal Detection of AI-Generated Images via Robustness Asymmetry

author.name: Xinchang Wang, Yunhao Chen, Yuechen Zhang, Congcong Bian, Zihao Guo, Xingjun Ma, Hui Li

entry.summary: RA-Det identifies 'robustness asymmetry' - natural images maintain stable representations under perturbations while AI-generated images show larger feature drift - as a universal behavioral signal for detecting AI-generated images.

entry.title: Jailbreaking Embodied LLMs via Action-level Manipulation

author.name: Xinyu Huang, Qiang Yang, Leming Shen, Zijing Ma, Yuanqing Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces Blindfold, an automated attack framework that exploits limited causal reasoning of embodied LLMs, showing that semantically benign instructions can lead to dangerous physical actions. Reveals misalignment between linguistic safety and physical outcomes.

entry.title: In-context learning of representations can be explained by induction circuits

author.name: Andy Arditi

entry.summary: Argues that the in-context representation geometry observed in LLMs processing random walks on graphs can be explained by well-known induction circuits (bigram recall), offering a simpler mechanism than previously suggested. Published as ICLR 2026 blogpost.

entry.title: Explaining undesirable model behavior: (How) can influence functions help?

author.name: Zhijing Jin

entry.summary: A technical overview of influence functions (IFs) for tracing undesirable LLM outputs back to specific training data points. Reviews recent advances in scaling IFs to 52B+ parameter models and discusses their potential as a mechanistic tool for identifying sources of bias and misalignment in frontier models trained on web-scale data.

entry.title: The Global Landscape of Environmental AI Regulation: From the Cost of Reasoning to a Right to Green AI

author.name: Kai Ebert, Boris Gamazaychikov, Philipp Hacker, Sasha Luccioni

entry.summary: Maps the global regulatory landscape of environmental AI governance across eleven jurisdictions, finding major gaps: facility-level rather than model-level governance, focus on training rather than inference, and limited AI-specific energy disclosure. Notes reasoning models have much higher environmental costs.

entry.title: Intrinsic Task Symmetry Drives Generalization in Algorithmic Tasks

author.name: Hyeonbin Hwang, Yeachan Park

entry.summary: Proposes that intrinsic task symmetries drive the grokking phenomenon, identifying a three-stage dynamic: memorization, symmetry acquisition, and geometric organization. Validated across diverse algorithmic domains.

entry.title: Constrained Particle Seeking: Solving Diffusion Inverse Problems with Just Forward Passes

author.name: Hongkun Dou, Zike Chen, Zeyu Li, Hongjue Li, Lijun Yang, Yue Deng

entry.summary: Constrained Particle Seeking (CPS) is a gradient-free approach for solving diffusion inverse problems that uses particle information to search for optimal candidates while incorporating constraints from the unconditional prior.

entry.title: Temporal Representations for Exploration: Learning Complex Exploratory Behavior without Extrinsic Rewards

author.name: Faisal Mohamed, Catherine Ji, Benjamin Eysenbach, Glen Berseth

entry.summary: Proposes using temporal contrastive representations to guide exploration in RL, prioritizing states with unpredictable future outcomes to enable complex exploratory behaviors without extrinsic rewards.

entry.title: GrapHist: Graph Self-Supervised Learning for Histopathology

author.name: Sevda \"O\u{g}\"ut, C\'edric Vincent-Cuaz, Natalia Dubljevic, Carlos Hurtado, Vaishnavi Subramanian, Pascal Frossard, Dorina Thanou

entry.summary: GrapHist introduces a graph-based self-supervised learning framework for histopathology that models tissues as cell graphs with masked autoencoders and heterophilic GNNs to learn biologically-informed embeddings.

entry.title: Measuring What AI Systems Might Do: Towards A Measurement Science in AI

author.name: Konstantinos Voudouris, Mirko Thalmann, Alex Kipnis, Jos\'e Hern\'andez-Orallo, Eric Schulz

entry.summary: Argues that AI capabilities and propensities are dispositional properties requiring rigorous measurement science, proposing a framework for operationalizing what AI systems are disposed to do rather than just observing performance.

entry.title: Rate-Distortion Signatures of Generalization and Information Trade-offs

author.name: Leyla Roksan Caglar, Pedro A. M. Mediano, Baihan Lin

entry.summary: Introduces a rate-distortion theoretic framework for comparing generalization in human and machine vision systems. Derives geometric signatures (slope and curvature) from confusion matrices to characterize accuracy-robustness trade-offs.

entry.title: Leave-One-Out Prediction for General Hypothesis Classes

author.name: Jian Qian, Jiachen Xu

entry.summary: Introduces MLSA, a general aggregation procedure for leave-one-out prediction that provides multiplicative oracle inequalities for arbitrary fixed datasets and losses satisfying mild monotonicity conditions.

entry.title: How Large Language Models Get Stuck: Early structure with persistent errors

author.name: Alokesh Manna, William Snyder, Whitney Tabor

entry.summary: Studies LLM training dynamics on BabyLM data, finding that in ~1/3 of BLiMP grammatical classes, the model establishes erroneous likelihood separations early and maintains them throughout training.

entry.title: FACE: A Face-based Autoregressive Representation for High-Fidelity and Efficient Mesh Generation

author.name: Hanxiao Wang, Yuan-Chen Guo, Ying-Tian Liu, Zi-Xin Zou, Biao Zhang, Weize Quan, Ding Liang, Yan-Pei Cao, Dong-Ming Yan

entry.summary: FACE introduces a face-level autoregressive mesh generation approach where each triangle face is one token, reducing sequence length by 9x and achieving 0.11 compression ratio, halving previous best.

entry.title: How Well Do Multimodal Models Reason on ECG Signals?

author.name: Maxwell A. Xu, Harish Haresumadram, Catherine W. Liu, Patrick Langer, Jathurshan Pradeepkumar, Wanting Mao, Sunita J. Ferns, Aradhana Verma, Jimeng Sun, Paul Schmiedmayer, Xin Liu, Daniel McDuff, Emily B. Fox, James M. Rehg

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for evaluating multimodal LLM reasoning on ECG signals by decomposing it into Perception (pattern identification) and Deduction (logical application of domain knowledge). Provides reproducible evaluation of clinical reasoning quality beyond QA metrics.

entry.title: DenoiseFlow: Uncertainty-Aware Denoising for Reliable LLM Agentic Workflows

author.name: Yandong Yan, Junwei Peng, Shijie Li, Chenxi Li, Yifei Shang, Can Deng, Ruiting Dai, Yongqiang Zhao, Jiaqi Zhu, Yu Huang

entry.summary: Proposes DenoiseFlow, which formalizes multi-step agent reasoning as a Noisy MDP to address accumulated semantic ambiguity - where minor interpretation errors compound across steps. Uses uncertainty-aware denoising for runtime adaptivity.

entry.title: SWE-Hub: A Unified Production System for Scalable, Executable Software Engineering Tasks

author.name: Yucheng Zeng, Shupeng Li, Daxiang Dong, Ruijie Xu, Zimo Chen, Liwei Zheng, Yuxuan Li, Zhe Zhou, Haotian Zhao, Lun Tian, Heng Xiao, Tianshu Zhu, Longkun Hao, Jianmin Wu

entry.summary: Introduces SWE-Hub, an end-to-end system for generating executable, scalable software engineering tasks including environment automation, scalable bug synthesis, and diverse task generation across languages.

entry.title: InfoPO: Information-Driven Policy Optimization for User-Centric Agents

author.name: Fanqi Kong, Jiayi Zhang, Mingyi Deng, Chenglin Wu, Yuyu Luo, Bang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces InfoPO (Information-Driven Policy Optimization) which frames multi-turn agent interaction as active uncertainty reduction, computing information-gain rewards to credit turns that measurably change agent behavior.

entry.title: MetaMind: General and Cognitive World Models in Multi-Agent Systems by Meta-Theory of Mind

author.name: Lingyi Wang, Rashed Shelim, Walid Saad, Naren Ramakrishna

entry.summary: Proposes MetaMind, a meta-theory of mind framework for world models in multi-agent systems where agents learn bidirectional inference (predict behavior from beliefs AND infer beliefs from behavior) in a self-supervised manner.

entry.title: Agents Learn Their Runtime: Interpreter Persistence as Training-Time Semantics

author.name: Victor May, Aaditya Salgarkar, Yishan Wang, Diganta Misra, Huu Nguyen

entry.summary: Isolates runtime state persistence as a training-time variable, showing models can learn to exploit interpreter persistence when training data exposes execution semantics. Introduces Opaque Knapsack benchmark to test this.

entry.title: ASTRA-bench: Evaluating Tool-Use Agent Reasoning and Action Planning with Personal User Context

author.name: Zidi Xiu, David Q. Sun, Kevin Cheng, Maitrik Patel, Josh Date, Yizhe Zhang, Jiarui Lu, Omar Attia, Raviteja Vemulapalli, Oncel Tuzel, Meng Cao, Samy Bengio

entry.summary: Presents ASTRA-bench for evaluating tool-use agents with time-evolving personal context, testing on state-of-art models including Claude-4.5-Opus and DeepSeek-V3.2, revealing performance degradation under high complexity.

entry.title: Scaling Tasks, Not Samples: Mastering Humanoid Control through Multi-Task Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shaohuai Liu, Weirui Ye, Yilun Du, Le Xie

entry.summary: Argues for scaling tasks rather than samples in model-based RL for humanoid control, showing shared world models benefit from multi-task experience while model-free methods suffer gradient interference across tasks.

entry.title: What Papers Don't Tell You: Recovering Tacit Knowledge for Automated Paper Reproduction

author.name: Lehui Li, Ruining Wang, Haochen Song, Yaoxin Mao, Tong Zhang, Yuyao Wang, Jiayi Fan, Yitong Zhang, Jieping Ye, Chengqi Zhang, Yongshun Gong

entry.summary: Formalizes the challenge of recovering tacit knowledge (relational, somatic, collective) that papers leave implicit when automating paper reproduction, and proposes a graph-based agent framework with dedicated mechanisms for each type.

entry.title: Rich Insights from Cheap Signals: Efficient Evaluations via Tensor Factorization

author.name: Felipe Maia Polo, Aida Nematzadeh, Virginia Aglietti, Adam Fisch, Isabela Albuquerque

entry.summary: Proposes a tensor factorization-based statistical model that merges cheap automated rater data with limited human gold-standard labels to enable fine-grained, prompt-level evaluation of generative models, overcoming the data bottleneck in detailed evaluation.

entry.title: Pencil Puzzle Bench: A Benchmark for Multi-Step Verifiable Reasoning

author.name: Justin Waugh

entry.summary: Introduces Pencil Puzzle Bench, a reasoning benchmark using 62,231 constraint-satisfaction puzzles across 94 varieties with deterministic step-level verification. Evaluates 51 models across 11 providers in both single-shot and agentic modes.

entry.title: The Value Sensitivity Gap: How Clinical Large Language Models Respond to Patient Preference Statements in Shared Decision-Making

author.name: Sanjay Basu

entry.summary: Conducts a factorial experiment testing how four LLM families (GPT-5.2, Claude 4.5 Sonnet, Gemini 3 Pro, DeepSeek-R1) respond to patient value statements in clinical decision-making across 98,759 encounter notes. Finds varying value sensitivity indices.

entry.title: Agentic Hives: Equilibrium, Indeterminacy, and Endogenous Cycles in Self-Organizing Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jean-Philippe Garnier (Br.AI.K)

entry.summary: Introduces 'Agentic Hive', a framework where variable populations of autonomous micro-agents undergo demographic dynamics (birth, death, specialization) governed by economic equilibrium theory inspired by Walrasian economics. Proves existence of equilibrium and endogenous cycles.

entry.title: NNiT: Width-Agnostic Neural Network Generation with Structurally Aligned Weight Spaces

author.name: Jiwoo Kim, Swarajh Mehta, Hao-Lun Hsu, Hyunwoo Ryu, Yudong Liu, Miroslav Pajic

entry.summary: NNiT generates neural network weights in a width-agnostic manner using patch-based tokenization and diffusion transformers, leveraging Graph HyperNetworks for structural alignment of the weight space.

entry.title: Your Inference Request Will Become a Black Box: Confidential Inference for Cloud-based Large Language Models

author.name: Chung-ju Huang, Huiqiang Zhao, Yuanpeng He, Lijian Li, Wenpin Jiao, Zhi Jin, Peixuan Chen, Leye Wang

entry.summary: Talaria is a confidential inference framework that partitions LLM pipelines to protect client data by executing sensitive operations in a Confidential Virtual Machine while offloading weight-dependent computations to cloud GPUs.

entry.title: Stateful Token Reduction for Long-Video Hybrid VLMs

author.name: Jindong Jiang, Amala Sanjay Deshmukh, Kateryna Chumachenko, Karan Sapra, Zhiding Yu, Guilin Liu, Andrew Tao, Pavlo Molchanov, Jan Kautz, Wonmin Byeon

entry.summary: Studies token reduction for hybrid VLMs (attention + Mamba), finding that while token importance is sparse within layers, the important tokens change across layers. Proposes progressive low-to-high compression strategy.

entry.title: TACIT Benchmark: A Programmatic Visual Reasoning Benchmark for Generative and Discriminative Models

author.name: Daniel Nobrega Medeiros

entry.summary: TACIT is a programmatic visual reasoning benchmark with 10 tasks across 6 reasoning domains, providing both generative and discriminative evaluation tracks with deterministic verification pipelines instead of LLM-as-judge.

entry.title: Challenges in Enabling Private Data Valuation

author.name: Yiwei Fu, Tianhao Wang, Varun Chandrasekaran

entry.summary: Analyzes the fundamental tension between differential privacy and data valuation, where DP requires insensitivity to individual records but valuation explicitly measures per-record influence.

entry.title: ROKA: Robust Knowledge Unlearning against Adversaries

author.name: Jinmyeong Shin, Joshua Tapia, Nicholas Ferreira, Gabriel Diaz, Moayed Daneshyari, Hyeran Jeon

entry.summary: ROKA introduces robust knowledge unlearning against indirect attacks that exploit knowledge contamination, modeling neural networks as Neural Knowledge Graphs and using graph-theoretic approaches for targeted unlearning.

entry.title: A Polynomial-Time Axiomatic Alternative to SHAP for Feature Attribution

author.name: Kazuhiro Hiraki, Shinichi Ishihara, Takumi Kongo, Junnosuke Shino

entry.summary: Proposes ESENSC_rev2, a polynomial-time alternative to SHAP for feature attribution grounded in cooperative game theory. It closely approximates exact SHAP values while being much more scalable.

entry.title: CaptionFool: Universal Image Captioning Model Attacks

author.name: Swapnil Parekh

entry.summary: CaptionFool demonstrates a universal adversarial attack on transformer-based image captioning models, achieving 94-96% success in generating arbitrary target captions by modifying only 1.2% of image patches, including content that evades moderation.

entry.title: ContextCov: Deriving and Enforcing Executable Constraints from Agent Instruction Files

author.name: Reshabh K Sharma

entry.summary: ContextCov transforms passive Agent Instructions (e.g., AGENTS.md) into active, executable guardrails that detect and prevent agent deviations ('Context Drift') from project-specific coding conventions.

entry.title: Artificial Superintelligence May be Useless: Equilibria in the Economy of Multiple AI Agents

author.name: Huan Cai, Ziqing Lu, Catherine Xu, Weiyu Xu, Jie Zheng

entry.summary: Analyzes economic equilibria in multi-agent economies with AI agents, showing that artificial superintelligence may provide no competitive advantage unless agents have exclusive capabilities, using Markov chain models.

entry.title: MM-DeepResearch: A Simple and Effective Multimodal Agentic Search Baseline

author.name: Huanjin Yao, Qixiang Yin, Min Yang, Ziwang Zhao, Yibo Wang, Haotian Luo, Jingyi Zhang, Jiaxing Huang

entry.summary: MM-DeepResearch develops a multimodal research agent with Hyper-Search (hypergraph-based QA generation) and DR-TTS for generating effective search trajectories for deep research tasks requiring cross-modal synthesis.

entry.title: ClinCoT: Clinical-Aware Visual Chain-of-Thought for Medical Vision Language Models

author.name: Xiwei Liu, Yulong Li, Xinlin Zhuang, Xuhui Li, Jianxu Chen, Haolin Yang, Imran Razzak, Yutong Xie

entry.summary: ClinCoT proposes a clinical-aware visual chain-of-thought framework that transforms preference optimization from response-level to visual-driven reasoning for medical VLMs. It grounds intermediate reasoning steps in localized pathological evidence to reduce hallucinations.

entry.title: Spectral Attention Steering for Prompt Highlighting

author.name: Weixian Waylon Li, Yuchen Niu, Yongxin Yang, Keshuang Li, Tiejun Ma, Shay B. Cohen

entry.summary: SEKA introduces a training-free attention steering method that edits key embeddings via spectral decomposition before attention computation, making it compatible with FlashAttention for prompt highlighting.

entry.title: Inference-Time Safety For Code LLMs Via Retrieval-Augmented Revision

author.name: Manisha Mukherjee, Vincent J. Hellendoorn

entry.summary: Proposes retrieval-augmented inference-time safety for code LLMs that surfaces relevant security risks and retrieves related security discussions to fix unsafe code without retraining.

entry.title: Pri4R: Learning World Dynamics for Vision-Language-Action Models with Privileged 4D Representation

author.name: Jisoo Kim, Jungbin Cho, Sanghyeok Chu, Ananya Bal, Jinhyung Kim, Gunhee Lee, Sihaeng Lee, Seung Hwan Kim, Bohyung Han, Hyunmin Lee, Laszlo A. Jeni, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: Pri4R augments VLA models with privileged 4D information (3D point tracks) during training to teach implicit understanding of world dynamics, using a lightweight point track head for joint prediction.

entry.title: Extracting Training Dialogue Data from Large Language Model based Task Bots

author.name: Shuo Zhang, Junzhou Zhao, Junji Hou, Pinghui Wang, Chenxu Wang, Jing Tao

entry.summary: Systematically studies how LLM memorization is inherited in task-oriented dialogue systems, demonstrating that training data including complete dialogue events can be extracted from LLM-based task bots.

entry.title: SafeSci: Safety Evaluation of Large Language Models in Science Domains and Beyond

author.name: Xiangyang Zhu, Yuan Tian, Qi Jia, Kaiwei Zhang, Zicheng Zhang, Chunyi Li, Kaiyuan Ji, Dongrui Liu, Zijian Chen, Lu Sun, Renrui Zhang, Yan Teng, Jing Shao, Wei Sun, Xia Hu, Yu Qiao, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: SafeSci introduces a comprehensive framework for safety evaluation in scientific domains with SafeSciBench (0.25M samples) and SafeSciTrain (1.5M samples), distinguishing safety knowledge from risk.

entry.title: DynaMoE: Dynamic Token-Level Expert Activation with Layer-Wise Adaptive Capacity for Mixture-of-Experts Neural Networks

author.name: G\"okdeniz G\"ulmez

entry.summary: Introduces DynaMoE, a Mixture-of-Experts framework that dynamically varies the number of active experts per token based on input complexity and adaptively allocates expert capacity across layers using six scheduling strategies.

entry.title: CHLU: The Causal Hamiltonian Learning Unit as a Symplectic Primitive for Deep Learning

author.name: Pratik Jawahar, Maurizio Pierini

entry.summary: Proposes the Causal Hamiltonian Learning Unit (CHLU), a physics-grounded neural network primitive using relativistic Hamiltonian structure and symplectic integration to conserve phase-space volume, addressing the memory-stability tradeoff in temporal modeling.

entry.title: Probabilistic Retrofitting of Learned Simulators

author.name: Cristiana Diaconu, Miles Cranmer, Richard E. Turner, Tanya Marwah, Payel Mukhopadhyay

entry.summary: Proposes probabilistic retrofitting of pre-trained deterministic PDE simulators using the CRPS scoring rule, transforming them into probabilistic models without retraining from scratch. Architecture-agnostic approach.

entry.title: Scaling Laws of SignSGD in Linear Regression: When Does It Outperform SGD?

author.name: Jihwan Kim, Dogyoon Song, Chulhee Yun

entry.summary: Analyzes scaling laws of signSGD under a power-law random features model, identifying drift-normalization and noise-reshaping effects. Shows signSGD can achieve steeper compute-optimal scaling than SGD in noise-dominated regimes.

entry.title: Scaling Retrieval Augmented Generation with RAG Fusion: Lessons from an Industry Deployment

author.name: Luigi Medrano, Arush Verma, Mukul Chhabra

entry.summary: Evaluates retrieval fusion techniques (multi-query retrieval, reciprocal rank fusion) in production RAG pipelines, finding that recall gains are largely neutralized after re-ranking under realistic constraints.

entry.title: A medical coding language model trained on clinical narratives from a population-wide cohort of 1.8 million patients

author.name: Joakim Edin, Sedrah Butt Balaganeshan, Annike Kj{\o}lby Kristensen, Lars Maal{\o}e, Ioannis Louloudis, S{\o}ren Brunak

entry.summary: Trains a medical coding language model on 5.8 million electronic health records from 1.8 million patients to predict ICD-10 codes from clinical notes, achieving 71.8% micro F1 and 95.5% top-10 recall, with analysis of performance variation across specialties.

entry.title: Stabilizing Policy Optimization via Logits Convexity

author.name: Hongzhan Chen, Tao Yang, Yuhua Zhu, Shiping Gao, Xiaojun Quan, Ting Yao

entry.summary: Investigates the stability gap between SFT and RL for LLMs from a gradient perspective, showing that SFT loss convexity w.r.t. logits enables stable training, and proposes a convexity-regularized PPO variant.

entry.title: Learn Hard Problems During RL with Reference Guided Fine-tuning

author.name: Yangzhen Wu, Shanda Li, Zixin Wen, Xin Zhou, Ameet Talwalkar, Yiming Yang, Wenhao Huang, Tianle Cai

entry.summary: Introduces Reference-Guided Fine-Tuning (ReGFT) that uses human-written reference solutions to synthesize positive trajectories on hard math problems before RL training, addressing reward sparsity for challenging problems.

entry.title: Invariant-Stratified Propagation for Expressive Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Asela Hevapathige, Ahad N. Zehmakan, Asiri Wijesinghe, Saman Halgamuge

entry.summary: Introduces Invariant-Stratified Propagation (ISP), a framework for GNNs that goes beyond the 1-WL expressivity limit while capturing structural heterogeneity. The approach provides both a novel WL variant and an efficient neural implementation.

entry.title: Practical Deep Heteroskedastic Regression

author.name: Mikkel Jordahn, Jonas Vestergaard Jensen, James Harrison, Michael Riis Andersen, Mikkel N. Schmidt

entry.summary: Identifies previously undiscussed practical challenges in deep heteroskedastic regression (optimization difficulties, representation collapse, variance overfitting) and proposes a simple procedure to address them.

entry.title: Trivial Graph Features and Classical Learning are Enough to Detect Random Anomalies

author.name: Matthieu Latapy, Stephany Rajeh

entry.summary: Demonstrates that trivial graph features combined with classical ML techniques can detect randomly injected anomalies in link streams extremely well, questioning the need for complex approaches in this common evaluation setting.

entry.title: Noise-Calibrated Inference from Differentially Private Sufficient Statistics in Exponential Families

author.name: Amir Asiaee, Samhita Pal

entry.summary: Develops noise-calibrated inference for differentially private sufficient statistics in exponential families, providing valid confidence intervals and optional synthetic data generation as post-processing.

entry.title: Tipping the Balance: Impact of Class Imbalance Correction on the Performance of Clinical Risk Prediction Models

author.name: Amalie Koch Andersen, Hadi Mehdizavareh, Arijit Khan, Tobias Becher, Simone Britsch, Markward Britsch, Morten B{\o}ttcher, Simon Winther, Palle Duun Rohde, Morten Hasselstr{\o}m Jensen, Simon Lebech Cichosz

entry.summary: Evaluates the impact of class imbalance correction techniques on both discrimination and calibration of clinical risk prediction models across 10 datasets with 605K patients, finding that resampling can harm calibration.

entry.title: Token Management in Multi-Tenant AI Inference Platforms

author.name: William J. Cunningham

entry.summary: Introduces 'token pools', a control-plane abstraction for multi-tenant AI inference platforms that represents capacity as explicit entitlements in inference-native units, unifying admission control and autoscaling.

entry.title: Initialization-Aware Score-Based Diffusion Sampling

author.name: Tiziano Fassina, Gabriel Cardoso, Sylvan Le Corff, Thomas Romary

entry.summary: Presents a theoretically grounded diffusion sampling strategy that learns the reverse-time initialization to reduce discretization steps. Provides KL convergence analysis showing the critical role of backward process initialization.

entry.title: Can AI Agents Agree?

author.name: Fr\'ed\'eric Berdoz, Leonardo Rugli, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: Evaluates LLM-based agents on Byzantine consensus games, finding that agreement is unreliable even in benign settings and degrades with group size and Byzantine agents. Failures are dominated by liveness issues.

entry.title: Causal Effects with Unobserved Unit Types in Interacting Human-AI Systems

author.name: William Overman, Sadegh Shirani, Mohsen Bayati

entry.summary: Studies causal effect estimation in interacting human-AI populations where unit types and network structure are unobserved. Uses causal message passing framework to estimate effects on humans in mixed human-AI systems.

entry.title: Quasar: Quantized Self-Speculative Acceleration for Rapid Inference via Memory-Efficient Verification

author.name: Guang Huang, Zeyi Wen

entry.summary: Quasar introduces quantized self-speculative decoding that addresses the verification bottleneck in speculative decoding by using quantized models for verification, achieving significant inference speedups training-free.

entry.title: Adaptive Spectral Feature Forecasting for Diffusion Sampling Acceleration

author.name: Jiaqi Han, Juntong Shi, Puheng Li, Haotian Ye, Qiushan Guo, Stefano Ermon

entry.summary: Spectrum proposes spectral diffusion feature forecasting for accelerating diffusion transformer inference, enabling global long-range feature reuse instead of local approximation used in caching approaches.

entry.title: Super Research: Answering Highly Complex Questions with Large Language Models through Super Deep and Super Wide Research

author.name: Yubo Dong, Nianhao You, Yuxuan Hou, Zixun Sun, Yue Zhang, Hehe Fan, Liang Zhang, Siyuan Zhao, Linyi

entry.summary: Introduces Super Research, a task and benchmark for highly complex autonomous research requiring 100+ retrieval steps and 1,000+ web pages, combining structured decomposition, wide retrieval, and deep iterative investigation.

entry.title: SkillCraft: Can LLM Agents Learn to Use Tools Skillfully?

author.name: Shiqi Chen, Jingze Gai, Ruochen Zhou, Jinghan Zhang, Tongyao Zhu, Junlong Li, Kangrui Wang, Zihan Wang, Zhengyu Chen, Klara Kaleb, Ning Miao, Siyang Gao, Cong Lu, Manling Li, Junxian He, Yee Whye Teh
